title: Live Stream Assertor, Telemetry, and Fallback Playbook for Constrained-Decoding
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Add a runtime 'Live Stream Assertor' component that continuously validates emitted token streams against active JSON-mode schemas and constrained-decoding expectations. The assertor will (1) emit structured telemetry when deviations are detected (token-level mismatch, truncated objects, unexpected terminals), (2) apply configurable remediation policies (retry with permissive decoder, invoke truncation-reassembly, fall back to synchronous full-response decoding, or route to a compatibility model), and (3) log minimal repro artifacts (prompt + stream prefix + model metadata) to a guarded bucket. This ticket covers the implementation of the assertor hook in the streaming pipeline, the telemetry schema and dashboards, a small policy engine for fallback decisions, and the accompanying e2e smoke and chaos tests that simulate partial streams and interleaved tool-calls.

2025-03-03 - Ravi P: Spike complete. Prototype hook implemented in runtime streaming handler; it can detect mismatched closing braces and missing required fields in small synthetic streams. Found two places where KV cache interference causes reordered tokens — added to edge-case list.

2025-03-05 - Design review (Jonas K): Approved telemetry fields but requested clearer opt-in controls for high-sensitivity customers. Suggested adding an org-level toggle and redaction rules for logged prompts.

2025-03-07 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 - implements assertor hook, basic policy engine, and unit tests for truncation-reassembly. CI failing on a flaky sampler test; investigating.

Added integration smoke suite and a Confluence doc with playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Live+Stream+Assertor+Playbook. Next: expand fuzz corpus and add canary rollout to dedicated pool before runtime-1.22 cut.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Assertor emits telemetry (stream_assertor.event) on mismatch with fields: error_type, token_index, model, route, and schema_id. 2) Fallback policy executes and returns a valid JSON payload or a documented failure path for >95% of injected partial-stream testcases. 3) Playbook documented and QA-run attached. 4) No P0 regressions in streaming latency during canary (p95 increase <= 1.5x for fallbacked requests).
test_plan: - Unit tests for parser-detectors and policy decisions. - Integration harness: synthetic generator for truncated objects, interleaved toolcall tokens, and slow network. - Chaos run in staging with 10k streamed requests. - Canary release to dedicated-qa pool with telemetry gating.
notes: Keep logged artifacts minimal and PII-free; coordinate with security for redaction rules before enabling artifact capture for production tenants. Ensure policy engine is configurable per-org to satisfy enterprise opt-outs.
